summary: S. 3546, titled the "Sunset Section 230 Act," repeals Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 entirely and updates various other federal laws to remove references and definitions tied to Section 230, replacing them with alternative references where necessary. The repeal and related amendments take effect two years after the date of enactment.

affected_groups.effect: They are subject to the repeal of Section 230 and related changes in federal statutes that reference interactive computer services and internet definitions.
affected_groups.group: Interactive computer service and internet-related providers

key_provisions: Repeals Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 in its entirety.
Updates the definition of "interactive computer service" within the Communications Act of 1934.

Removes references to Section 230 from multiple other statutes, including the Trademark Act of 1946, Title 17, Title 18, the Controlled Substances Act, the Webb-Kenyon Act, Title 28, Title 31, and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act.
Establishes an effective date for all repeal provisions and conforming amendments that is two years after the date of enactment.
